papers.what_it_is: A short Quantum Computing Inc web lesson page claiming quantum computers threaten public-key cryptography and that QKD alone is insufficient, listing three use cases.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Public-Private Key scheme is constructed assuming the intractability of some mathematical problems, such as finding large integers' prime factors (RSA) or computing integer pairs satisfying the curve equation (ECC).
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: In a nutshell, PPK is constructed assuming the intractability of some mathematical problems like finding large integers' prime factors (e.g., in RSA), or computing integer pairs satisfying the curve equation (e.g., in ECC).
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors state that PPK-based protocols are generally considered secure because no efficient algorithm is known to solve those problems on current digital computers.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: The PPK-based protocols are generally considered to be secure as there is no known efficient algorithm to solve those math problems in current digital computers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors claim that quantum computers will defeat current cryptographic algorithms and decrypt data while it is being transmitted.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: Quantum computers will defeat current cryptographic algorithms and decrypt data while it is being transmitted.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors claim that quantum computers will be able to defeat cryptographic hash functions by implementing fast search algorithms.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: However, quantum computers will be able to defeat this approach by implementing fast search algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors claim that quantum computers will defeat authentication algorithms, making data transmission vulnerable to interception or diversion and enabling malicious parties to penetrate the communication chain.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: Quantum computers will defeat authentication algorithms thereby making data transmission vulnerable to being intercepted/diverted or enabling malicious parties to penetrate the communication chain.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors claim that an adversary armed with a quantum computer can easily forge digital signatures and fake certificates.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: An adversary armed with a quantum computer can easily forge digital signatures and fake certificates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors state that random numbers are a vital ingredient in all cryptographic algorithms, that random number generators produce encryption keys, and that increasing randomness or entropy is essential to the future of secure communications.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: Random number generators are used to produce encryption keys.
Increasing the randomness/entropy is essential to the future of secure communications.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors claim that quantum computers' ability to crack encryption and authentication protocols will invalidate the premises on which privacy-preserving computing schemes rely.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: will invalidate the premises on which privacy-preserving computing schemes rely
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors state that, despite many efforts to replace PPK with post quantum cryptography methods, none has been proven secure against future quantum algorithms.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: Even though many efforts have been invested to replace PPK using post quantum cryptography methods, none has been proven to be secure against future quantum algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors state that Quantum Key Distribution is not enough to defend communication networks in the quantum era, because it solves only the distribution of encryption keys and guarantees only the security of data-in-transit even when running ideally.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: QKD focuses on solving only one problem, the distribution of encryption keys.
Even if running ideally, a QKD-based network can only guarantee the security of data-in-transit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The authors state that authentication, verification and digital signatures still rely on classical cryptography in a QKD network and are thus vulnerable to quantum computer attacks.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: authentication, verification, and digital signatures, still rely on classical cryptography and are thus vulnerable to quantum computer attacks
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: QCi states that it is building an end-to-end quantum solution to defend the security of the digital world against quantum computer attacks.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: QCi is building an end-to-end quantum solution to defend the security of our digital world against quantum computer attacks with the following use cases.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.
assertions.reader_inference: No product, protocol or result is described on the page.

assertions.value: The page lists secure multi-party computation as a use case: distrusted parties compare and perform a secure computation on their combined data without revealing their personal data.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: A pool of distrusted parties wish to compare and perform a secure computation on their combined data without revealing their perspective personal data.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The page lists user authentication as a use case: a credit card user proves identity by showing knowledge of the secret password without revealing it.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: A credit card user must prove her identity by showing she knows the secret password without revealing her actual password.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.

assertions.value: The page lists private blockchain transaction as a use case: a user performs a zero-knowledge proof to process a blockchain transaction while remaining anonymous.
assertions.anchor: Cybersecurity under quantum computer threats, p.1
quotes: A user wishes to perform zero-knowledge proof to process a transaction on a blockchain while remaining anonymous.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without evidence in a vendor lesson page.
